title: underscoreHeadersStrategy replaced by aliasHeadersStrategy

detection.reason: checked in the Traefik workload's container args only (Deployment or DaemonSet) — an option set through a static configuration file or environment variables is not scanned

quote: From version `v3.7.12` onwards, a new `aliasHeadersStrategy` entry point option deprecates and replaces the `underscoreHeadersStrategy` option introduced in `v3.6.20`.
remediation: Move the entry point from `underscoreHeadersStrategy` to `aliasHeadersStrategy` (the first release carrying it is v3.6.22 on the changelog, not the v3.6.20 the guide names, and no 3.6 release has `aliasHeadersStrategy`). The default `keep` changes nothing for traffic. The break to avoid is setting BOTH options on one entry point with different values: Traefik then rejects the install configuration (`cannot have both underscoreHeadersStrategy and aliasHeadersStrategy options configured with different values`) and does not start. The replacement also covers every aliasing character, not only the underscore — re-check the header names you accept before choosing `delete` or `reject`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.args[]? | tostring | test("underscoreHeadersStrategy")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed still set the deprecated option; also check Helm values and any static config ConfigMap

title: BasicAuth middleware without users unmounts its routers

detection.reason: the Middleware projection names each Middleware's TYPE (`types[]`), so the Middlewares of this type are named as candidates — but whether one is affected depends on its configuration body, which the projection does not carry, so the item cannot be settled

quote: From version `v3.7.3` onwards, the BasicAuth middleware requires a non-empty users configuration in order to be built successfully. Previously, the middleware would be built successfully but always return a 401 status code for any request. Now, an error occurs and any routers using it will be unmounted. For the same request, a 404 status code is served instead of a 401 status code.
remediation: Give every BasicAuth middleware a non-empty `users` list (or a `secret` reference that resolves to users) before upgrading. This is a behaviour change with real blast radius: a middleware that previously just returned 401 now fails to build, and every router referencing it is unmounted — those routes return 404 rather than prompting for credentials.
verifyCommand: kubectl get middlewares.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.basicAuth != null) | select(((.spec.basicAuth.users // []) | length) == 0 and (.spec.basicAuth.secret // "") == "") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed have no users and will unmount their routers

title: A default TLSOption or TLSStore in any namespace is cluster-wide

detection.reason: TLSOption and TLSStore are not among the collected kinds (IngressRoute, IngressRouteTCP and Middleware), so their existence cannot be read from the synced inventory

quote: In the Kubernetes CRD provider, the `TLSOption` and the `TLSStore` named `default` are cluster-wide, whatever the namespace they are defined in. Anyone allowed to create one in a single namespace can therefore replace the TLS policy, mutual TLS authentication included, of the routers that do not reference TLS options explicitly.
remediation: Treat the ability to create a TLSOption or TLSStore named `default` as a cluster-wide privilege and restrict it with RBAC. Audit which namespaces can create them today, and have security-sensitive routers reference their TLS options explicitly rather than relying on the default, so a default defined elsewhere cannot silently weaken them.
verifyCommand: kubectl get tlsoptions.traefik.io,tlsstores.traefik.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "default") | .kind + " " + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # any row is a cluster-wide default owned by that namespace

title: CRDs must be updated for the new retry options and ingressClassName

detection.reason: this is about the CRD SCHEMA shipped with Traefik rather than about any collected object's contents

quote: To use the new options of the `retry` middleware or the new `ingressClassName` field with the Kubernetes CRD provider, you need to update your CRDs.
remediation: Apply the v3.7 CRD manifests before using the new `retry` options or `ingressClassName`. Until the CRDs are updated the API server strips or rejects those fields, so the configuration appears to apply while having no effect.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd middlewares.traefik.io -o json | jq -e '.spec.versions[].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties.retry' >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "retry present in CRD schema" || echo "CRD schema predates the new retry options"

title: crossProviderNamespaces controls cross-provider references

detection.reason: this is Traefik static/provider configuration, not a field on any collected Kubernetes object

quote: In `v3.7.1`, a new `crossProviderNamespaces` option is available on the Kubernetes CRD, Ingress, and Gateway providers.
remediation: Decide this deliberately rather than inheriting the default. The option governs whether resources in one provider may reference resources in another; enabling it widens what a namespace owner can reach across provider boundaries.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)(mirrored-library-|library-)?traefik([:@]|$)"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) replicas=\(.spec.replicas // "per-node")", (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.args // [])[]), (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.env // [])[] | "env \(.name)")' | grep -iE '^(Deployment|DaemonSet) |crossProviderNamespaces' # rows show whether crossProviderNamespaces is set on the providers; nothing printed means the default applies, decide it explicitly; a static configuration file mounted from a ConfigMap is not listed, read it too

title: errorRequestHeaders needs updated CRDs to be usable

detection.reason: the Middleware projection names each Middleware's TYPE (`types[]`), so the Middlewares of this type are named as candidates — but whether one is affected depends on its configuration body, which the projection does not carry, so the item cannot be settled

quote: The `errorRequestHeaders` option, introduced in `v3.6.15` for the Errors middleware, was not exposed on the Kubernetes CRD provider. Starting with `v3.7.8`, it can now be configured on the `Middleware` CRD.
remediation: Apply the updated CRD manifest for this Traefik minor BEFORE upgrading if you intend to use `errorRequestHeaders` on the Errors middleware. Until the CRD carries the field the API server strips it, so the option appears to apply and silently does nothing.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd middlewares.traefik.io -o json | jq -e '.spec.versions[].schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties.errors.properties.errorRequestHeaders' >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "errorRequestHeaders present in CRD schema" || echo "CRD schema predates errorRequestHeaders"

title: Gateway API provider moves to spec v1.5.1

detection.reason: the installed Gateway API bundle version lives in an annotation on the Gateway API CRDs, and CRD objects are collected as served versions without their metadata

quote: Starting with `v3.7.0`, the Kubernetes Gateway API provider supports version v1.5.1 of the specification, which requires the Gateway API CRDs to be updated.
remediation: Update the Gateway API CRDs to v1.5.1 or later BEFORE upgrading Traefik. The 3.7 provider always watches TLSRoute v1 and BackendTLSPolicy v1, which older bundles do not serve, and Traefik documents what an unserved watched version does: the Kubernetes Gateway provider never completes its startup, so NO Gateway API route is served — not just the new kinds — and no error is logged while Traefik keeps running. A related change needs no action: the provider's Kubernetes client QPS/Burst rise to 50/100 from v3.7.3. The v3.7.10 move to spec v1.6.1 is its own item.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.gateway\.networking\.k8s\.io/bundle-version}{"\n"}' # must be v1.5.1 or later

title: Gateway API v1.6.1 Standard CRDs stop serving TCPRoute v1alpha2 — the Gateway provider never starts

detection.reason: which Gateway API channel the CRDs were installed from, and their served versions of TCPRoute, live in CRD metadata the agent does not collect

quote: Starting with `v3.7.10`, the Kubernetes Gateway API provider supports version v1.6.1 of the specification.
remediation: Traefik 3.7 still watches TCPRoute through v1alpha2, which the v1.6.x Standard channel CRDs no longer serve. If you use TCPRoute and move the CRDs to v1.6.1, install the EXPERIMENTAL channel CRDs — otherwise the Kubernetes Gateway provider never completes its startup and no Gateway API resource is served at all, with no error logged. Traefik 3.7 stays compatible with the v1.5.x CRDs, so not upgrading the CRDs is also safe.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd tcproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions[*].name}{"\n"}' 2>/dev/null # if TCPRoute is in use, v1alpha2 must still be listed (experimental channel); no such CRD means nothing to check

title: Gateway API generated router names change their hash suffix

detection.reason: the routers this note describes are generated by Traefik at runtime from Gateway API objects; they are not Kubernetes objects the agent can collect

quote: Starting with `v3.7.10`, the Kubernetes Gateway API provider derives the hash suffix of the router names it generates from all the route, Gateway, and listener identifying fields, instead of from the route rule alone.
remediation: Generated router names change on upgrade. Update anything that pins them — dashboards, metrics queries and alert rules built on router-name labels stop matching silently. The change itself prevents distinct routes colliding onto one generated router name.
verifyCommand: kubectl get httproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io,tcproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io,tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A 2>/dev/null # every route listed gets a new generated router name on upgrade; nothing listed (or no such CRDs) means the Gateway provider has nothing to rename

title: Gateway API generated service and middleware names gain the route rule prefix

detection.reason: the services and middlewares this note describes are generated by Traefik at runtime from Gateway API objects; they are not Kubernetes objects the agent can collect

quote: Starting with `v3.7.6`, the Kubernetes Gateway API provider derives the name of the services and middlewares it generates from the route rule they belong to, instead of from the backend reference alone.
remediation: Generated service and middleware names change on upgrade. Update anything that pins them — dashboards, metrics queries and alert rules built on service-name labels stop matching silently.
verifyCommand: kubectl get httproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io,tcproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io,tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A 2>/dev/null # every route listed gets new generated service and middleware names on upgrade; nothing listed (or no such CRDs) means the Gateway provider has nothing to rename

title: Upgrade: h2c and HTTP2-Settings request headers are no longer forwarded to backends

detection.reason: whether a backend relied on an h2c upgrade negotiated past Traefik is runtime protocol behaviour, not a property of any collected object

quote: Starting with `v3.7.13`, Traefik does not forward the `Upgrade: h2c` and `HTTP2-Settings` request headers to the backends anymore.
remediation: A backend that accepted such an upgrade now serves those requests over HTTP/1.1. To keep cleartext HTTP/2 to a backend, declare it with the h2c scheme (`scheme: h2c` on the IngressRoute service, or the `traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/service.serversscheme: h2c` Ingress annotation).
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]?.services[]? | select(.scheme == "h2c") | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  " + .name' # services printed already use h2c with prior knowledge and are unaffected

title: HTTP/1 CONNECT requests now return 501

detection.reason: this is request-time protocol behaviour, not a property of any collected object

quote: Starting with `v3.7.9`, HTTP/1 `CONNECT` requests are rejected with a `501 Not Implemented` response.
remediation: No action for almost every deployment: HTTP/1 CONNECT was non-functional before this change, so the rejection makes existing behaviour explicit rather than removing a capability. Only investigate if a client genuinely issues HTTP/1 CONNECT to Traefik.

title: Ingress NGINX provider needs a configmaps RBAC grant

detection.reason: this is a grant on Traefik's own ClusterRole, which is not among the collected kinds

quote: Starting with `v3.7.0`, the Ingress NGINX provider now supports the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/custom-headers` annotation to add custom headers to the response forwarded to the client.
remediation: Add the `configmaps` permission to the KubernetesIngressNGINX provider's RBAC. The annotation reads its header values from a ConfigMap, so without the grant the annotation is accepted and silently has no effect.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterrole -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.rules[]?.resources[]? == "ingresses") | .metadata.name as $n | .rules[] | select(.resources[]? == "configmaps") | $n' # a name confirms the configmaps grant is present

title: Requests with a rootless target (http:example.com/admin) are rejected with 400

detection.reason: this is request-time protocol behaviour, not a property of any collected object

quote: Starting with `v3.7.13`, a request whose target is rootless, that is a target made of a scheme followed by something that does not start with a slash, is rejected with a `400 Bad Request` response.
remediation: No action for normal clients: such a target is none of the forms HTTP/1.1 allows, and it escaped the path handling and routing rules. Only investigate if a client starts receiving 400s after the upgrade.

title: safeNaming changes generated router, middleware and service names

detection.reason: this is Traefik static/provider configuration, not a field on any collected Kubernetes object

quote: Starting with `v3.7.11`, the new `safeNaming` provider option enables collision-safe naming for the routers, middlewares and services generated by the Kubernetes CRD provider, instead of the current naming scheme, under which names can collide across namespaces or resources.
remediation: Enabling `safeNaming` is the safer configuration, but it renames the generated routers, middlewares and services. Anything that references those generated names — dashboards, metrics queries, alerting rules, API scripts — has to be updated in the same change. Leaving it off keeps a real collision risk across namespaces.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)(mirrored-library-|library-)?traefik([:@]|$)"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) replicas=\(.spec.replicas // "per-node")", (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.args // [])[]), (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.env // [])[] | "env \(.name)")' | grep -iE '^(Deployment|DaemonSet) |safeNaming' # nothing printed means safeNaming is unset; enabling it renames every generated router, middleware and service; a static configuration file mounted from a ConfigMap is not listed, read it too

title: New core.strictTLSOptions option can turn the silent default-TLS fallback into disabled routers

detection.reason: core.strictTLSOptions is a static (install) option set through container args, Helm values or a static config file; whether two routers actually conflict is the live Traefik risk rule tls-options-conflict, which names the routes

quote: Starting with `v3.7.11`, the new `core.strictTLSOptions` install configuration option disables this fallback: the routers involved in the conflict are marked in error and are not built at all.
remediation: Nothing changes on upgrade: a host served on one entry point with different TLS options already falls back to the `default` options, and still does. This release adds core.strictTLSOptions, which disables the conflicting routers instead. Check the Risk tab for tls-options-conflict first — enabling the option while a conflict exists takes those routers down.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.args[]?] | map(tostring) | any(test("(?i)strictTLSOptions"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed already set core.strictTLSOptions; also check Helm values and any static config file

title: StripPrefix returns 400 when the stripped path is not normalised

detection.reason: the Middleware projection names each Middleware's TYPE (`types[]`), so the Middlewares of this type are named as candidates — but whether one is affected depends on its configuration body, which the projection does not carry, so the item cannot be settled

quote: From version `v3.7.3` onwards, the StripPrefix middleware and the StripPrefixRegex middleware reject requests (`400 Bad Request`) when stripping the configured prefix produces a path that differs from its normalised form (i.e. a path containing `.` or `..` segments that would be collapsed by normalisation).
remediation: Check any client or upstream that relies on `.`/`..` segments surviving a StripPrefix. Those requests now get a 400 instead of being forwarded. This is a hardening change, so the right fix is normally to fix the caller's path rather than to work around it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get middlewares.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.stripPrefix != null or .spec.stripPrefixRegex != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + "  " + ((.spec.stripPrefix.prefixes // .spec.stripPrefixRegex.regex // []) | join(","))' # names printed strip a prefix; a caller whose path still carries . or .. segments after stripping now receives 400

title: Negative weights in TCP/UDP weighted services are now rejected

detection.reason: the IngressRouteTCP projection carries each route service's weight; IngressRouteUDP is not collected, so a negative UDP weight is not checked

quote: Negative weights in a TCP or UDP weighted service are now rejected when the service is built. Such a configuration previously made the load-balancer selection loop endlessly while holding its lock, which consumed a CPU core and blocked every subsequent connection to that service until Traefik was restarted.
remediation: Remove any negative weight from TCP and UDP weighted services before upgrading — the service now fails to build instead of being accepted. This one is worth fixing regardless of the upgrade: on earlier versions the same configuration pins a CPU core and blocks every subsequent connection to that service until Traefik restarts.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutetcps.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]?.services[]? | select((.weight // 0) < 0) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  weight=" + (.weight|tostring)' # rows printed fail to build in 3.7

title: A weighted service with an unbuildable child now reports disabled

detection.reason: the setting lives on a service under spec.routes[].services[], nested inside the routes array rather than at the top level of the projection

quote: When a child of a TCP or UDP weighted service cannot be built, for instance because it does not exist, the parent weighted service is now reported as `disabled` in the API, with the error attached, as the HTTP weighted service already was.
remediation: No configuration change is required — this only changes what the API reports. Note it when debugging: a TCP/UDP weighted service whose child is missing now shows as `disabled` with the error attached, where before it reported neither an error nor a status. The routers referencing it were already not created either way.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutetcps.traefik.io,ingressrouteudps.traefik.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $r | .spec.routes[]? | select((.services // [])[1] != null) | .services[] | "\($r.kind) \($r.metadata.namespace)/\($r.metadata.name) child \(.namespace // $r.metadata.namespace)/\(.name):\(.port)"' # every child Service printed must exist; a missing child now marks the parent weighted service disabled in the API

title: Host(`*`) now matches every request, including requests with no host
quote: From version `v3.7.7` onwards, the `Host` matcher treats a bare `*` as a catch-all, consistent with the TCP `HostSNI(`*`)` matcher. ``Host(`*`)`` now matches every request regardless of its host, including requests with no host at all.
remediation: Find any router whose rule uses a bare ``Host(`*`)`` and confirm catch-all is what you intend. Before 3.7.7 such a rule matched far less; after it, that router can capture traffic meant for more specific routers, and priority becomes the only thing keeping them apart.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]? | select(.match | test("Host\\(`\\*`\\)")) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  " + .match' # rows printed become catch-all routers in 3.7.7+

title: Host and HostSNI gain single-level wildcard subdomain matching
quote: Since `v3.7.0`, the `Host` and `HostSNI` matchers support wildcard subdomain matching (e.g., `*.example.com`). This allows matching any direct subdomain of a domain with a single-level wildcard prefix. For example, `*.example.com` matches `foo.example.com` but not `foo.bar.example.com` or `example.com` itself.
remediation: If any rule already contains a literal `*.` host, confirm the new semantics match what you intended: it now matches exactly one level of subdomain — not the apex, and not deeper subdomains. Routers that previously never matched such traffic may start receiving it; for an IngressRouteTCP router using ``HostSNI(`*.example.com`)`` that is TLS connections for every direct subdomain.

title: Ingress-NGINX provider keeps dots in generated router and service names

detection.reason: the change is in the names Traefik generates from Ingress and Secret names; an Ingress name is metadata, which no spec-path rule reads

quote: Starting with `v3.7.14`, the resource names are kept as is: the router of an Ingress named `my.ingress` is now `default-my.ingress-rule-0-path-0` instead of `default-my-ingress-rule-0-path-0`. Dashboards, alerts and API queries relying on the previous names must be updated.
remediation: Traffic is unchanged. Update dashboards, alerts and API queries that name routers, services, serversTransports or TLS options generated for an Ingress or Secret whose name contains a dot, and for Ingresses with `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-passthrough` (their HTTP routers are renamed after the rule and path). Two Ingresses named `my.ingress` and `my-ingress` no longer collide, so the one that was silently overridden starts serving.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | contains(".")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed get new generated router names at 3.7.14

title: Gateway API: of two routes that match equally well, only the one with precedence serves

detection.reason: the coded check rtz-traefik-gateway-equal-rule-route-not-served compares HTTPRoutes and GRPCRoutes per listener and rule when the agent ships their resolved parents and match digests; TLSRoutes and TCPRoutes, and routes whose listeners or matches are not fully known, are not compared

quote: Starting with `v3.7.14`, only the route that has precedence serves the requests. The specification gives precedence to the older route, then to the first route in alphabetical order by `{namespace}/{name}`. Traefik does not create the routers of the other routes.
remediation: Find routes attached to the same listener that produce the same rule — typically one route with no host name and one with the listener's host name. Before 3.7.14 either could serve (and it could change at each reload); from 3.7.14 the older route, then the alphabetically first `{namespace}/{name}`, always serves and the other gets no router. If the app team relies on the route that loses, give it a distinct match (host, path or header) before upgrading. Traefik logs a warning naming the router that serves the rule.
verifyCommand: kubectl get httproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | [(.spec.parentRefs // [] | map(.name + "/" + (.sectionName // "*")) | join(",")), (.spec.hostnames // [] | join(",")), .metadata.creationTimestamp, .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name] | @tsv' | sort # routes on the same parent/listener with the same match: only the oldest serves at 3.7.14

title: Gateway API: TLSRoute router and service names change

detection.reason: the change is in router and service names Traefik generates, which no collected object carries; the coded check rtz-traefik-gateway-tlsroute-router-names-change names the served TLSRoutes

quote: Starting with `v3.7.14`, the hash suffix of the TLSRoute router names is also derived from the router rule, so the names of all the TLSRoute routers, and of the services derived from them, change.
remediation: Update dashboards, alerts and API queries that name TLSRoute routers or their services. A TLSRoute attached to several TLS listeners on one entry point previously kept only one router; from 3.7.14 every listener gets its own, so passthrough traffic that was silently dropped on the other listeners starts being served.
verifyCommand: kubectl get tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A -o name 2>/dev/null # every TLSRoute listed gets new router and service names at 3.7.14

title: OpenTelemetry request-duration histograms follow the exponential-aggregation environment variable

detection.reason: the switch is an environment variable's VALUE, and the agent sends environment variable names only

quote: Starting with `v3.7.14`, these histograms follow this environment variable, and the `metrics.otlp.explicitBoundaries` option only applies to explicit bucket histograms.
remediation: Operators only — no traffic effect. If the Traefik pod sets `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_DEFAULT_HISTOGRAM_AGGREGATION=base2_exponential_bucket_histogram`, the `traefik_*_request_duration_seconds` histograms switch from explicit buckets to exponential ones: update dashboards and alerts that read the bucket series.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]?.name] | index("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_DEFAULT_HISTOGRAM_AGGREGATION")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # workloads printed set the variable; check its value

title: Ingress router.pathmatcher accepts only Path, PathPrefix and PathRegexp

detection.reason: checked the router.pathmatcher annotation's value on Ingress

gate.reason: Traefik reads the annotation only for paths whose pathType is ImplementationSpecific; Prefix and Exact paths ignore it

quote: **[k8s/ingress]** Avoid ingress path matcher injection and backport 11d251415 ([#13227](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/pull/13227) @rtribotte)
remediation: Set the annotation to `Path`, `PathPrefix` or `PathRegexp` (exact case), or remove it. From these patches Traefik refuses any other value ("invalid router path matcher"), logs "Skipping path." and builds no router for that path, so the Ingress's ImplementationSpecific paths answer 404 after the upgrade. A value that worked before by being pasted into the rule (`pathprefix`, `Host`, `Query`) is what breaks; a value that never parsed was already 404.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | (.metadata.annotations // {})["traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.pathmatcher"] as $m | select($m != null and ($m | IN("Path","PathPrefix","PathRegexp") | not)) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + "  " + $m' # Ingresses printed are skipped after the upgrade

title: Backends behind ingress-nginx basic or digest auth stop receiving Authorization

detection.reason: checked the nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-type annotation's value on Ingress

gate.reason: only Traefik's Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider translates these annotations; with the provider off, Traefik never reads them

quote: **[k8s/ingress-nginx]** Remove Authorization header for basic and digest auth  ([#13631](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/pull/13631) @josmo)
remediation: Traefik now mirrors ingress-nginx and removes the `Authorization` header before the request reaches the backend of an Ingress protected by basic or digest auth. A backend that reads the user from that header (or forwards it to another service) loses it at the upgrade: pass the identity another way, for example with `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-url` and a response header, before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.metadata.annotations // {})["nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-type"] | IN("basic","digest")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # backends of the Ingresses printed stop receiving Authorization

title: Routes with their own TLS options answer 421 more often when SNI and Host differ

detection.reason: whether a client sends no SNI, or an SNI that differs from its Host header, is decided per request; the routes it can affect are named

quote: **[server]** Move snicheck to ctx instead of simulated routing ([#13214](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/pull/13214) @juliens)
remediation: For routes that use a non-default TLSOption, Traefik now checks the SNI against the Host header on the request itself, so clients that send no SNI or reuse one connection for several hosts (HTTP/2 connection coalescing, some health checkers and proxies) get `421 Misdirected Request`. Test those clients against the upgraded controller, and make them send an SNI that matches the Host.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.tls.options != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + "  options=" + .spec.tls.options.name' # routes printed enforce SNI = Host for their TLS options

title: A route's TLSOption now applies to its wildcard Host

detection.reason: the change bites only where a wildcard Host or HostSNI route also names a TLSOption that is stricter than the default; one predicate cannot test both, so the wildcard routes are named

quote: Since `v3.7.0`, TLSOptions can now be associated with routers using wildcard `Host` and `HostSNI` matchers (e.g., `Host(`*.example.com`)`).
remediation: Before v3.7 such a router fell back to the default TLS options with a warning. From v3.7 the route's own TLSOption applies, so a stricter minVersion, cipher list or client-certificate requirement (mTLS) starts being enforced on the wildcard hosts. Check the clients of these routes against the TLSOption they name.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.tls.options != null) | . as $o | .spec.routes[]? | select(.match | test("Host\\(\\s*[`\"]\\*\\.")) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  options=" + $o.spec.tls.options.name' # routes printed start enforcing their TLSOption on wildcard hosts

title: CORS headers change: no Max-Age 0 by default, wildcard with credentials reflects the origin

detection.reason: the difference shows in browser preflight behaviour per origin; the Middlewares that configure CORS are named

quote: **[middleware]** Fix CORS Max-Age set to 0 by default ([#13371](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/pull/13371) @AnatoleLucet)
remediation: Two CORS fixes land together. Traefik no longer sends `Access-Control-Max-Age: 0` when `accessControlMaxAge` is unset, so browsers start caching preflights for their own default. And a wildcard origin list combined with `accessControlAllowCredentials: true` now answers with the requesting origin, which browsers accept, instead of `*`, which they reject, so cross-origin credentialed calls that used to fail start succeeding. Review both for the Middlewares named.
verifyCommand: kubectl get middlewares.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.headers.accessControlAllowOriginList != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + "  credentials=" + ((.spec.headers.accessControlAllowCredentials // false) | tostring) + " maxAge=" + ((.spec.headers.accessControlMaxAge // "unset") | tostring)' # Middlewares printed send different CORS headers
